newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Labour still in the coalition running -Cullen.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Labour still in the coalition running -Cullen.

text.p: Labour Party deputy leader Michael Cullen on Tuesday discounted mounting speculation that National will form the next government with nationalist New Zealand First.

Recent media reports suggest National Party insiders are growing increasingly optimistic that New Zealand First will soon select the conservative National caretaker government as its preferred coalition partner.
But centre-left Labour is insisting it remains a serious prospect to form the next government.
Cullen told Radio New Zealand that New Zealand First was still bargaining in good faith with Labour.

"I certainly believe New Zealand First is bargaining in good faith. A great deal of time is going into this, additional meetings are being organised, not necessarily at the most convenient times for either party.
"I don't believe they'd be doing that if they had already made up their minds," he said.
Cullen expects the next government will be formed by December 10, Radio NZ reported.
Nationalist New Zealand First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating separately with National and Labour over the shape of the new government.
